metadata.title: Tre' Harris - No work Wednesday
metadata.description: Harris (hamstring) was listed as a non-participant on Wednesday's injury report.
metadata.analysis: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Harris is week-to-week with the injury he sustained in Sunday's loss to the Broncos, so it comes as little surprise that he did not see any action Wednesday.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris (hamstring) considered week-to-week
metadata.description: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Tre' Harris is "more of a week-to-week [thing]."
metadata.analysis: Harris will likely be targeting a return in Week 8 following the Chargers bye.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris Still Worth Stashing Despite Hamstring Injury?
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Tre' Harris (hamstring) was a sneaky pickup going into the Week 5 game against the division-rival Denver Broncos on Sunday, with both Ladd McConkey (foot) and Quentin Johnston (chest) questionable to play. McConkey was active (did not end up playing any snaps), while Johnston was held out. It was shaping up to be a high-target day for Harris in the Chargers' banged-up offense, but L.A.'s offense continued to struggle before Harris left the game in the second half and never returned due to a hamstring injury. He caught two of his four targets for only 16 yards before departing. With McConkey, Johnston, and Harris all injured, tight end Charlie Kolar ended up leading the Chargers in receiving with three grabs on four targets for only 37 yards on a day in which quarterback Justin Herbert threw for only 121 yards. Harris is now considered week-to-week with his hamstring injury, meaning he could miss the Week 6 divisional clash against the Kansas City Chiefs. Keep in mind that the Chargers' bye comes in Week 7 when deciding whether to keep Harris stashed as WR depth in deeper fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris - Considered week-to-week
metadata.description: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Harris is "week-to-week" due to a hamstring injury that he sustained during Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Harris entered Sunday as the Chargers' WR1 due to the absence of Quentin Johnston (chest) while Ladd McConkey (foot) was available only as an emergency option, per Insdorf. Harris caught two of four passes for 16 yards before sustaining a hamstring injury, which was severe enough for him to not return. Given Harbaugh's update, coupled with the Chargers' bye scheduled for Week 7, it seems likely that Harris will be held out for Week 6 against the Chiefs, with an eye toward being available for Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1. Given the Chargers' injuries to the wide receiver position, the team will need to lean more heavily on Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Theo Wease, Derius Davis and tight ends Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden in the passing game.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris Considered "Week-to-Week"
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh called wide receiver Tre' Harris (hamstring) "more week-to-week" on Monday, according to Alex Insdorf. Harris was in line for a bigger workload in the Week 5 divisional tilt against the Denver Broncos on Sunday with Ladd McConkey (foot) banged up and Quentin Johnston (chest) ruled out, but he ended up playing only 45% of the offensive snaps in the 23-17 loss after tweaking his hamstring in the second half. Harris finished with just two catches on four targets for a season-low 16 receiving yards. The 24-year-old should probably be considered more doubtful than questionable to play this weekend against the division-rival Kansas City Chiefs, especially with the Chargers' bye coming in Week 7. If Harris does not get the green light to play in Week 6, his next opportunity to suit up will not come until Nov. 1 against the Los Angeles Rams. Harris currently has 15 receptions on 25 targets for 225 yards and no touchdowns in his first five games of his sophomore campaign in 2026.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris does little in Week 5 loss
metadata.description: Tre' Harris came up with 2-of-4 targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos.
metadata.analysis: Harris was basically the de facto No. 1 WR for the Chargers on Sunday. However, he didn't do much and actually ended up sustaining a hamstring injury along the way. Harris had been on the ascent the last couple of weeks, but the Chargers' offense is just an absolute mess right now.  Harris will need to be monitored at practice this week before visiting Kansas City.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris - Dealing with hamstring injury
metadata.description: Harris (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
metadata.analysis: Harris is dealing with an apparent hamstring injury, and his availability for the stretch run of Sunday's matchup is now up in the air. In his absence, Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Derius Davis will likely slot into more prominent roles on offense.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris Questionable to Return with Hamstring Injury
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Tre' Harris (hamstring) is questionable to return with a hamstring injury. The wideout drew just four targets before leaving the game and caught only two for 16 yards. Harris was expected to take on a lead role this afternoon with Quentin Johnston (chest) inactive and Ladd McConkey (foot) on a strict snap count. For now, managers should expect tight ends Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden to be Justin Herbert's top options in the passing attack.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris a Viable Flex Play in Week 5 vs. Broncos
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wideout Tre' Harris could see a bigger role in Sunday's Week 5 matchup against the division-rival Denver Broncos. The Chargers ruled out wideout Quentin Johnston (chest) and listed Ladd McConkey (foot) as questionable. Harris has quietly broken out over the past few weeks and has led the team in receiving yards each week since Week 2. He has steadily taken over the WR2 role for the Chargers and is one injury away from becoming the WR1. Harris enters Week 5 as RotoBaller's PPR WR45 in an intriguing matchup. The Broncos' defense will be without its top 2 cornerbacks, Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss, and has allowed the 13th-most passing yards and the 14th-most passing touchdowns. Harris can be plugged into flex spots for managers battling injuries and bye weeks.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris - Set to be Bolts' WR1 against Denver
metadata.description: Harris' workload should be larger against the Broncos on Sunday, as Quentin Johnston (chest) has been ruled out and Ladd McConkey (foot, questionable) may not play, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Rookie fourth-rounder Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) has also been ruled out alongside Johnston. McConkey faces an uphill battle to play Sunday after sitting out of practice all week, and he may operate under a snap count if he's given the green light to suit up. That puts Harris -- who has seen five targets or more in three of four games this season -- in position to work in an elevated role against a Broncos defense that will be without both starting outside cornerbacks Riley Moss (ribs) and Patrick Surtain (ankle).

metadata.title: Tre' Harris a Must-Roster Player with Teammate Injured
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Tre' Harris has been the team's leading receiver this season and could see an even bigger role in Week 5. Through four games, Harris has caught 13 of 21 targets for 209 yards, including more than 60 yards in back-to-back games. In last week's 30-23 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, Harris played 66 of 71 snaps (93%) and ran 39 of 43 routes (91%), both leading the team. With Ladd McConkey (foot) uncertain to play in Week 5, Harris could become Justin Herbert's clear number one receiver. With the Denver Broncos next up and star cornerback Pat Surtain (ankle) unlikely to play, Harris could be in line for a solid outing in Week 5. Fantasy managers should add Harris as both a short-term and long-term option this season.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris - Notches 60 yards in loss
metadata.description: Harris caught three of five targets for 60 yards during Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seahawks.
metadata.analysis: Harris led the team in receiving yards for the second straight week, recording at least 53 receiving yards for the third contest in a row. Ladd McConkey (foot) aggravated his pre-existing foot injury in the contest, and he is considered week-to-week for the time being. If McConkey is unavailable in Week 5 versus the Broncos, Harris may have a chance to operate as the team's primary pass-catcher.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris totals 60 yards Sunday
metadata.description: Tre' Harris caught 3-of-5 targets for 60 yards in the Chargers 30-23 loss against the Seahawks.
metadata.analysis: Harris was the leading receiver for Justin Herbert and the Chargers on the day. He'll be a flex play next week if Ladd McConkey (foot) is sidelined.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris Faces Tough Test After Recent Surge
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Tre' Harris has been one of the few bright spots in the passing game over the last two weeks. He led the team with 53 receiving yards in Week 2 on one catch, then followed that with six receptions for 76 yards on seven targets in Buffalo. Harris now has 10 catches for 149 yards on 16 targets through three games, and his 76 yards last week were a regular-season career high. Ladd McConkey (foot) is questionable for Sunday, so Harris could have another chance to stay involved if McConkey is limited or unavailable. The problem is the matchup. Seattle has allowed the fewest receiving yards to wide receivers this season and has been especially good at limiting explosive plays. Harris sits at WR57 in RotoBaller's latest Week 4 rankings. His recent production has earned attention, but this is still a difficult spot to trust him outside deeper leagues.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris is Gaining Trust After Solid Performance
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Tre' Harris was able to break out during this past weekend's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Harris was fairly quiet during the first two games of the year, but he made a solid impact on Sunday. Harris hauled in six of his seven targets for 76 yards in the loss to the Bills. Both the receptions and receiving yards are new season high for Harris. The hope is that this good performance will lead to more opportunities for Harris during the Week 4 matchup against the New England Patriots. Harris is worth a look in deep leagues after this six-catch performance.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris - Leads team in receiving in defeat
metadata.description: Harris caught six of seven targets for 76 yards during Sunday's 24-16 loss to Buffalo.
metadata.analysis: Harris led the team in targets, receptions and receiving yards in the loss, all of which represented new career highs for the second-year pro. The wide receiver has now reeled in 10 of 16 targets for 149 yards over three games to open the regular season, and he appears to be on track to be a pivotal member of the team's passing attack in 2026.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris leads pass-catchers in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Tre' Harris hauled in six of his team-high seven targets for 76 yards in the Chargers' 24-16 Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
metadata.analysis: Harris has capitalized on inconsistent usage in the Los Angeles offense of late, leading the team in receiving yards in each of the last two games. The wideout remains one of the more stable pass-catching options as part of an underwhelming Chargers offense to begin the season, with a Week 4 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks up next.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris Hopes to Expand His Role in Week 3 vs. Bills
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wideout Tre' Harris is coming off his best NFL performance after leading the team in receiving yards last week. The 24-year-old produced a 53-yard play on a critical third down, putting the team in the red zone and giving fantasy managers a glimpse of his upside if he can take his game to the next level. Harris enters Week 3 as RotoBaller's WR68 in an intriguing matchup. The Bills defense has allowed the 3rd-most 20-plus-yard passes (9) and the 5th-most passing yards. In addition, the Bills defense ranks near the bottom of the league in EPA and has given up too many high-value plays. Harris has an opportunity for back-to-back solid outings, which could lead to a permanent expanded role. The Ole Miss product should remain out of fantasy lineups for now, but could become a reliable flex option in deep leagues this season.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris - Secures long catch in loss
metadata.description: Harris caught one of three targets for 53 yards during Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders.
metadata.analysis: Harris was the Chargers' only starting wide receiver in the contest with Ladd McConkey dealing with a ribs injury. Harris played 56 of the team's 68 offensive snaps, which was more than the next closest wide receivers Quentin Johnston (55) and McConkey (31). The 24-year-old wasn't able to rack up the catches, but he did make a major splash with his one snag, connecting with Justin Herbert for a 53-yard catch and run in the third quarter. Harris has now caught four of nine targets for 73 yards over the team's first two games of the season.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris leads team in receiving Sunday
metadata.description: Tre' Harris caught 1-of-3 targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
metadata.analysis: Harris was the leading receiver for the Chargers on Sunday, and he was able to earn that title with just one 53-yard catch on the afternoon. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high hopes for him moving forward after two underwhelming games to start the season.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris Leads Chargers in Receiving Yards in Week 2 Loss
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wideout Tre' Harris caught one of his three targets for 53 yards in Sunday's devastating 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. The 24-year-old had the Chargers' top play of the day on a critical third down that put the team in the red zone. The 53-yard play was a glimpse of Harris' big-play upside he possesses. However, the Ole Miss product continues to operate as the team's WR3 behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston. Through two weeks, Harris has caught four of his nine targets and has no touchdowns. He will remain an intriguing fantasy receiver in deep leagues but should remain off fantasy radars in standard-sized leagues. Harris and the Chargers will head on the road for the first time this season to face the Buffalo Bills in Week 3.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris on Deep-League Flex Radar vs. Raiders in Week 2
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wideout Tre' Harris offers intriguing upside on Sunday against the division-rival Las Vegas Raiders. Harris could be forced into the WR2 role with Ladd McConkey (ribs) being listed as questionable. McConkey exited Week 1 after taking a big hit and was held out of practice until participating in a limited amount on Friday. Harris enters Week 2 as RotoBaller's PPR WR70 in a favorable matchup against the Raiders' secondary. Raiders defense allowed 220 passing yards and five 20-plus-yard passing plays to a shaky Miami Dolphins passing game last week. This could be the opportunity Harris stockholders have been waiting for to see their fantasy investment break out in an expanded role. Harris is a viable flex option in deeper leagues and carries an unknown ceiling heading into Week 2.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris Could Have Bigger Opportunity With Teammate Injured
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Tre' Harris and the Chargers' offense surprisingly struggled to move the ball consistently in their Week 1 season-opening upset loss to the Arizona Cardinals. Harris caught half of his six targets on the day for just 20 yards and was held out of the end zone in the first game of his sophomore season in 2026. The good news for the former second-rounder from Mississippi is that he played a healthy 75% of the offensive snaps (just two fewer than Quentin Johnston). The 24-year-old pass-catcher has become an interesting waiver-wire option at receiver heading into a Week 2 divisional tilt against the Las Vegas Raiders, primarily because top wideout Ladd McConkey (rib) is currently questionable after missing Wednesday's practice. If McConkey is not cleared to play this weekend, Harris will have a significantly bigger role alongside Johnston and could be worth a flex play in deeper fantasy leagues. Harris caught 30 passes for 324 yards and one touchdown on 43 targets in 17 games as a rookie in 2025.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris - Logs three catches Week 1
metadata.description: Harris caught three of six targets for 20 yards in Sunday's loss to Arizona.
metadata.analysis: Harris tied for the second-most targets on his team, but he couldn't do much with those looks. Fellow wideout Quentin Johnston didn't do any better, catching just two of his six targets for 17 yards, yet both wideouts might be asked to step up if Ladd McConkey (ribs) isn't able to play next Sunday versus Las Vegas. Harris also logged nine special-teams snaps Sunday, but he wasn't a major contributor in that regard last season.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris on the Waiver Radar After Teammate's Injury in Week 1
metadata.description: The Los Angeles Chargers' offense was not impressive in the surprising 26-14 Week 1 season-opening loss to the visiting Arizona Cardinals on Sunday at SoFi Stadium. Second-year wide receiver Tre' Harris finished the game with three catches on his six targets for 20 yards. Wideout Ladd McConkey (rib) was the only Chargers receiver to find the end zone, finishing his day with five catches for a team-high 82 yards and a touchdown, but he left the game early with a rib injury and did not return. Although Harris' final line was not impressive at all, he did play 75% of the offensive snaps, which was second only to Quentin Johnston, and his six targets were only one off the team lead (seven for McConkey). If McConkey's rib injury causes him to miss time, Harris will undoubtedly have a bigger role in Mike McDaniel's passing attack, which will be looking to bounce back in Week 2 versus the division-rival Las Vegas Raiders. Harris is a speculative waiver-wire pickup this week in deeper leagues for managers who have McConkey rostered or who are already searching for better WR depth. He is rostered in only 4% of Yahoo leagues.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris finishes with three receptions in Week 1
metadata.description: Tre' Harris caught 3-of-6 targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
metadata.analysis: Harris was at least significantly involved in the passing game Sunday, as the second-year wideout tied a career high in targets set in Week 18 of last season. Harris did not do much with those targets, however, totaling only 20 yards with a long of 11. The second-round pick from 2025 is a fringe redraft option at present.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris Remains Hidden in Crowded Offense for Week 1
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wideout Tre' Harris had a quiet offseason heading into his sophomore campaign, even though his offense was often discussed with the arrival of Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator. McDaniel is viewed as an offensive guru who has called plays for some of the most explosive offenses over the last few seasons. However, Harris has been overlooked by analysts even as they have attempted to get as much exposure to the offense as possible. The 24-year-old will likely be deployed as the WR3 in the Chargers' offense that has heavy target competition with Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, Charlie Kolar, Omarion Hampton, and Keaton Mitchell all vying for targets. Harris is RotoBaller's PPR WR72 in a favorable matchup against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. The Cardinals defense allowed the sixth-most passing touchdowns (31), ninth-most completions (375), and 10th-most passing yards (4,128) last season. Harris should remain out of fantasy lineups in Week 1 and should be viewed only as a touchdown-dependent flex option for managers in a tough spot in deeper leagues.

metadata.title: Tre' Harris - Fully healthy for Week 1
metadata.description: Harris (undisclosed) is not listed on the Week 1 injury report Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Harris dealt with an unspecified injury last month but is fine for Sunday's season opener against the Cardinals. He's expected to fill the WR3 role behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnson this season, but the Chargers also figure to use plenty of TE-heavy sets with Charlie Kolar, Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku.
